title: A message from Kontigo's CEO: 10 months of investigation & enhancements:
summary: A message from Kontigo's CEO: 10 months of investigation & enhancements
body_markdown:
## Where we come from, and Why Kontigo


Kontigo was created to address a deeply personal problem experienced by our founding team, our families, and all our friends in our home countries. We grew up in Venezuela, Colombia, Argentina, and Mexico. Collectively, they add up to an astonishing hyperinflation percentage and over 200M underbanked humans. Our early life was capped from opportunities due to financial exclusion.


Thanks to a lot of hard work, we escaped the spiral and moved to San Francisco under the O-1 Visa for *extraordinary ability* , but we still have our closest people trapped in a never-ending economic vicious cycle.


Kontigo is focused on serving the estimated 500 million people in Latin America that are underbanked.Kontigo’s core mission is to help individuals and small businesses in Latin America who lack meaningful access to traditional banking infrastructure, especially those facing spiraling inflation and rapid depreciation of local currency, to obtain access to and hold stablecoin, and to access remittances, currency exchange, and yield services through Kontigo and its partners.


I started building financial tools to overcome the economic crisis in my country when I was 15 and came to the US because it was the promised land to make a real global impact. Kontigo has always been my personal obsession: providing opportunities to hundreds of millions by giving them access to basic financial technologies.


### **The chronology of events**


Earlier this year, questions were raised publicly regarding some of Kontigo’s services in Venezuela. We acted fast and took those allegations seriously. Strong compliance with U.S. and other laws has always been a core aspect of our business model. We undertook a rigorous and in-depth review over the last 10 months, partnering with top tier law firms and forensic specialists.


At the time these reports emerged, our compliance program already included substantial controls, such as (a) full identification and verification for fiat transactions; (b) liveness/ “deepfake” checks, (c) source of funds KYC on users who engage in transactions above certain monetary thresholds; (d) in-depth Know-Your Business, or KYB, diligence on entity users; and (e) screening of users using a third-party sanctions screening vendor.


For the past 10 months, we have been dedicated to two things and two things only: (1) working with experienced external legal counsel, forensic specialists, and compliance advisers to conduct an extensive review of our operations and compliance structure; and (2) attending to our now 3.4 million underbanked customers and their billions in annualized transaction volume through the Kontigo App.


As we previously announced, Kontigo commissioned a review led by top tier external legal counsel, forensic specialists, and compliance advisers, and added additional resources for Kontigo’s legal, compliance, and cybersecurity teams, including:


- Crowell & Moring LLP, a leading AmLaw 100 firm *Chambers* ranked for its digital assets and sanctions practices, to review our compliance with U.S. sanctions.Their team is led by former U.S. government officials from OFAC, FinCEN, and DOJ.
- StoneTurn, a leading global advisory firm consistently ranked in *Chambers* for its forensic accounting, asset tracing, and business intelligence practices, to assist in reviewing our historical transactions.
- A *Chambers* -ranked, leading Latin American law firm as local Venezuelan external counsel, with one of its partners joining Kontigo as our Outside General Counsel & Interim Sanctions Compliance Officer.
- A new Head of Banking & Compliance Operations, a person with previous experience at a Y Combinator-backed fintech regulated in the US.


Together, these advisers assisted Kontigo in evaluating the relevant facts, sanctions considerations, and identifying any needed improvements to our existing compliance controls, even as we continued to pursue our broader mission of attending to the 3.4 million underbanked customers that now use the Kontigo App.


With the advice of our compliance team, we have implemented a number of enhancements to our already strong program, including:


- Improved automated sanctions screening of transactions, including User Banks in Venezuela that Originate or Receive VES exchanged for USDC or USDT
- Enhanced Beneficial Ownership Identification Thresholds for Certain High-Risk Jurisdictions
- Enhanced geographic, device and jurisdictional screening controls
- Enhanced Partner Diligence and Regular Sanctions Screening of Partners
- The appointment of an interim Sanctions Compliance Officer (currently Kontigo’s Outside General Counsel, who is also an attorney in private practice at a *Chambers* ranked law firm in Venezuela), as well as establishing requirements for sanctions compliance training and regular independent audits of the Kontigo sanctions compliance program.
- Improvements to our written sanctions compliance program


The review is now complete.Like all companies operating in the financial services and financial technology space, we identified areas for improvement.We also identified shortcomings where we could have operated better.At the same time, the review did not find information to support many of the allegations that have been made.In particular,the review:


- Did not identify information indicating intentional efforts by Kontigo to evade US sanctions.
- Did not find any connection between Kontigo and the former President of Venezuela or his family.
- Did not identify any customers of Kontigo that were sanctioned.


Furthermore, many of the allegations related to persons sending transactions through certain sanctioned banks, such as Banco de Venezuela and Banco del Tesoro, without considering that OFAC has since 2019 had general licenses in place that allow “U.S. Persons” – individuals and entities -- to maintain accounts at thesebanks, allow U.S. and non-U.S. persons to send non-commercial remittances through these banks, and allow major credit card companies and money transmitters to conduct transactions through them.Furthermore, in April of 2026, just a few months after the allegations were reported, OFAC provided even broader authorization for dealings with these banks through its general license 57, which also allows dealings with the Central Bank of Venezuela.We have worked closely with our legal advisors to ensure our activities now comport with these authorizations.


Both now and in the past, OFAC has made clear that its sanctions are not intended to prevent day-to-day transactions by the Venezuelan people, as expressed extensively in multiple OFAC general licenses, FAQs, executive orders and guidance documents. Nor is Venezuela itself subject to comprehensive sanctions (like those against Iran, Cuba, or North Korea).


Because aspects of the review and related legal matters remain confidential, we are limited in the additional detail we can share publicly..Regardless, we have worked with our external advisors to take our existing compliance program – which was already strong – and make it even stronger alongside a key strategy of regulatory engagement.


Throughout this process, Kontigo has remained focused on establishing the facts through a comprehensive review conducted with the assistance of outside counsel and forensic specialists.


Importantly, Kontigo has always sought, and continues to seek, to get things right.It is incorporated in the United States, and unlike many in the digital assets space, it does not offer “No KYC” services, nor do we permit transactions involving comprehensively-sanctioned jurisdictions.We are committed to offering services to the underserved and underbanked, particularly in Latin America, but in a legally compliant manner.On this front, the U.S. government has strongly encouraged digital assets and FinTech innovation, and Kontigo views itself as a key part of that.We will continue to review our program for ways we can make it best-in-class.


### **Dedicated Compliance Resources**


Kontigo has significantly expanded the internal and external resources supporting its compliance framework. The company works with specialized technology providers and professional advisers such as Blockaid and Seon for customer identification, transaction monitoring, risk controls, on-chain wallet screening, and Crowell & Moring as outside U.S. sanction compliance counsel, among many others.


Kontigo regularly evaluates its compliance systems, advisers, and service providers and remains committed to identifying and engaging best-in-class partners that can further strengthen its compliance structure as the company, its products, and the regulatory environment continue to evolve.


### **What Kontigo makes possible**


People and businesses from the global south access Kontigo because we're the best platform to help them escape their currency inflation. This is not another fancy stablecoin neobank. This is real skin in the game. We take people out of misery. We’re not in the game of crypto casinos, buy now pay maybe, speculation, and undifferentiated crypto-cards. We are serving real and urgent needs people have in their day-to-day lives, as a clear goal from day one.


We've purposefully focused on the countries where people need it the most, and we've designed the easiest and most understandable product UX to onboard millions. For them, stablecoins are not a new trend; they've been personally using them for the past 10 years, daily.


The regulatory compliance in these countries is extremely difficult, and we take it extremely seriously. That's why our obsessive commitment to self-custody, freedom and decentralization matters that much in these nations. For us, the product is crystal clear: a banking alternative that lives and runs 100% on the blockchain and in the user's device. A product where every click, every asset, and every currency is tokenized.


Although our users may not care about blockchain technology or tokenization, they do care about their ability to access financial services. The incentive structure of centralized global neobanks is completely different from the ones that have the blockchain as its main source of truth.


We believe that decentralized software, self-custody, and the newest intersection of AI x crypto are the technological breakthroughs that will evenly distribute opportunities in a world of superintelligence. That's where Kontigo stands.


### **About Venezuela: Why We Believe in Long-Term Opportunity**


Venezuela is the largest investment opportunity in the world at this moment. Not even Anthropic IPO has these multiples. We’re talking about several trillion dollars of upside, and downsides are incrementally decreasing every day. The exponential is several orders of magnitude from what it is today. It 's asymmetric.


The core multiplier in this equation is energy, the nation is in the global top 10 reserves for oil, natural gas, gold, aluminium, iron ore, rare minerals, hydropower and mining capacity, biodiversity, urbanization rate, educational attainment rate, caribbean coast-miles, amazon rainforest. And yes, we’ve also been the historical Miss Universe winners.


By becoming the US-primary energetic partner in the western hemisphere, Venezuela would irreversibly become the south-american Taiwan. We’ve the talent, the culture, the natural resources and now the capital and political conditions to do so.


Recent regulatory developments and growing international attention toward Venezuela may contribute to increased economic activity and financial innovation in the months ahead. Kontigo began building products for Venezuelan users long before renewed international interest in the country emerged because we believed the needs of individuals and businesses would eventually require modern financial infrastructure regardless of short-term market sentiment.


Kontigo launched in Venezuela three years before it was an evident consensus investment opportunity, like it’s becoming nowadays. The recent publication of OFAC’s[General License 57](https://ofac.treasury.gov/media/935516/download?inline) and the U.S. government approach to Venezuela more broadly widens the opportunity door for Kontigo to build the financial plumbing for the Venezuelan Golden Era.


Kontigo remains committed to supporting individuals and businesses in Venezuela through responsible, compliant, and accessible financial technology. We remain optimistic about the country's long-term future and look forward to sharing more about our plans in the coming weeks. Welcome to **Venezuelan Dynamism.**


**We're very excited about Kontigo's future. Although the past 10 months were not easy nor from a corporate level nor a personal one, we are grateful to our employees, users, partners and investors for their trust and patience throughout this process.**


**We are committed to building Kontigo responsibly for the long term, right from where we started, here in San Francisco, California.**


**Kontigo never left the arena!**


Jesus Castillo


**CEO & Co-founder**
